rationale: The assistant followed a sensible, safe path (overload check, then unplugged hand-turn of the drum) and correctly identified the drive belt as the likely cause with appropriate hedging, without inventing evidence or asserting part compatibility. However, it gave up as soon as the model number was only partial — it did not ask for the serial number, try another sticker location, use the TVHM8 prefix to narrow the belt, or ask about the noise at failure or look for the belt under the drum — and sent the customer to an engineer for a job that is reasonable DIY with power isolated. The customer leaves with a correct suspicion but no actionable fix path, after only half the available turns.
